summary: Richmond Hill, Dighton MA tower first operated 1912, staffed to 1915, moved to Rehoboth in 1915 or 1916; the Long Hill tower there is the 1931 replacement.

facts.design: Steel tower with 8'x8' cab and ladder; height given as 38 ft by the Forest Fire site and 28 ft by the Register and Forest Lookouts
facts.status_note: Tower moved from Richmond Hill to Rehoboth in 1915 or 1916; no source we read describes the Richmond Hill site today
facts.agency: Not named in the sources read

events.note: First operated in 1912 (Forest Fire site); Forest Lookouts says constructed 1912
Staffed until 1915 and discontinued that September (Forest Fire site)
Forest Fire Dighton page says moved to Rehoboth in 1915; Register, Forest Lookouts and Rehoboth Tower Site page say 1916
Moved to Great Meadow Hill in Rehoboth; Rehoboth Tower Site page says first operated there in 1916 after the move from Dighton
New 68-foot tower built on Great Meadow Hill to replace the older one
Register says the Army requested the move; Forest Fire Rehoboth page says the Army ordered the tower removed; the 1931 tower was rebuilt on Long Hill

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Fire Dighton page says the tower was moved to Rehoboth in 1915; the Register, Forest Lookouts and Forest Fire Rehoboth page say 1916. The story gives both.
Forest Fire Dighton page gives 38 ft; the Register and Forest Lookouts give 28 ft for the 1912 tower. facts.height_m is left out until the sources agree.
The Register says the Army requested the move; the Forest Fire Rehoboth page says the Army ordered removal.

notes_for_editor: Four sources agree on the 1912 start and the 1915/1916 move, but disagree on the year of the move and on the original height (38 ft vs 28 ft). The 1931 replacement tower is the one now on Long Hill per the Register and Forest Fire Rehoboth page; no source ties the original Dighton steel structure to any surviving tower. Richmond Hill site today is undescribed by sources read. FFLA Massachusetts Facebook posts about Richmond Hill and footings were found in search results but fetch returned titles only, so no claims from them are used. Consider cross-linking with the Rehoboth Tower Site #1 record.
